summary.headline: Cello World Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR654 crore (record quarter), but EBITDA margin fell to 20.9%; FY27 revenue guided at 10-12% growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was a record INR653.6 crore, up 11% YoY, with EBITDA of INR136.6 crore (20.9% margin) and PAT of INR90.1 crore (13.8% margin). FY26 revenue grew 8.8% to INR2,323.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR526.4 crore (22.7%) and PAT margin of 14.3%, weighed down by glassware losses and steel bottle ramp-up costs. Management described FY26 as a year of corrective initiatives and said Q1 FY27 looks challenging due to the Middle East-linked cost and demand headwinds. Steel bottle capacity is ramping in phases toward full scale by July 2026, and the Wimplast merger and a restructuring scheme took effect from 27 May 2026.

segments.name: Consumerware
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR434 crore (66.4% of total), up 7% YoY; gross margin 47.8%. Glassware sales grew without profit, and steel ware margins fell 5-6% due to shifting from China sourcing to costlier OEMs. Appliances sold out in March on LPG-driven demand.

segments.name: Writing instruments
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR128 crore (19.6% of total), up 64% YoY including Cello brand from Q4; excluding Cello, grew at a healthy double-digit rate. FY26 segment revenue about INR368 crore; FY27 target INR500 crore plus.

segments.name: Moulded furniture and allied
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about 14% of total; moulded furniture fell 13.5% YoY in line with industry demand. Wimplast merged into the company; gross margin 39.5%.

segments.name: Steel bottles (within consumerware)
segments.commentary: Sales fell 25% in FY26 due to capacity constraints, with stock-outs in insulated steel. Two lines running in Q4, four more in Q1 FY27 and two further lines expected soon; peak revenue of current capacity about INR300 crore.

segments.name: Glassware (within consumerware)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 60% due to Chinese dumping; segment at breakeven. Management targets peak revenue of about INR300 crore at 28-30% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Opalware (within consumerware)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 85%, leaving about 15% headroom; management plans to exhaust capacity before any expansion, which would need a greenfield site in Rajasthan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-12%, with management cautioning it could change as the year progresses; volume growth may be subdued while value growth holds.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 2-2.5 percentage points, driven by steel ware and glassware scale-up; consumerware margin improvement of about 2.5-3%.
Q1 FY27 expected to be challenging due to current crisis-related cost and demand headwinds; not seasonal.
Writing instruments FY27 revenue target INR500 crore plus; margins expected to recover over a couple of quarters toward Unomax levels.
FY27 capex about INR100 crore, mainly maintenance, with about INR30 crore for steel ware and building.
Debtor days target reduced by 10-15 days to under 100 days; steel bottle lines to reach full production from July 2026.
Management said return to 25-26% margins is achievable with steel, glassware and Cello pen recovery, if demand holds.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR219 crore, mainly steel bottle lines, other consumerware and writing instrument lines, plus maintenance.
Steel bottle lines: 2 commissioned in Q4 FY26, 4 more in Q1 FY27, and 2 more expected shortly; full-scale operation by July 2026. Peak revenue of current capacity about INR300 crore.
Glassware utilisation about 60%; management says peak revenue about INR300 crore and the plant has a 10-year furnace life.
Opalware utilisation about 85%; expansion would require greenfield capacity in a new Rajasthan hub, deferred until competition settles.
FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crore.
demand_pricing: MRP increases of 12-20% taken across product lines to pass on higher raw material, energy and labour costs; management expects some price correction later in the year.
Channel buying is cautious due to steep price rises, but channel inventory is improving; management expects Q1 to be weaker than Q4.
E-commerce and quick commerce now about 17% of revenue, with profitability in line with other segments.
Channel mix in Q4: general trade 75.4%, online 9.5%, export 7.6%, modern trade 7.5%.
Glassware faces dumping of imported Chinese products; company is seeking government protection.
Opalware faces new competition about 6-odd months old; management is cautious on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why was steel bottle capacity delayed from Q4 FY26 to Q2 FY27, and what is the revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no delay: lines started in phases, with 2 in Q4, 4 in Q1 FY27 and 2 more after. Steel ware sales fell about 25% in FY26 due to capacity constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance for revenue growth and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 10-12% and EBITDA margin up about 2-2.5 percentage points, with a possible change depending on the crisis.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin compression in consumerware and writing instruments in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Glassware revenue grew without profit, steel ware margin fell 5-6% from costlier OEM sourcing, and appliances carried lower margins. Cello pens were loss-making before the acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top-line guidance conservative given 12-20% MRP hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value growth will come, but volumes could be subdued this year. The price increases may not hold for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash is there and how will it be used? Any buyback plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is being held for adjacent inorganic opportunities with distribution or manufacturing synergies, which may depress return ratios. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to reduce receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to cut 15-odd days to under 100 days, through better channel inventory checks, distributor stock liquidation support and SKU rationalisation. Government tenders stretched receivables.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 expected to be weak with the Middle East-linked crisis and steep raw material and crude-linked cost increases; volume decline risk.
Glassware remains at about 60% utilisation and breakeven under Chinese dumping; protection outcome pending.
Steel bottle ramp-up to full scale by July 2026 is a key execution milestone.
Writing instruments margin recovery depends on cost cuts and product mix; gross margin fell in Q4.
Receivable days stretched by government tenders; target 15-odd days reduction.
Surplus cash and low return ratios; any inorganic deal would be a capital allocation test.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and structural initiatives, but cautious on near-term trading: management repeatedly flagged Q1 FY27 as challenging, with demand subdued and costs sharply higher. Management was evasive on the writing instruments revenue split and on how far price increases will hold.
key_quotes: For us, glassware remains a long-term strategic growth business rather than a near-term profit maximization opportunity.
Writing instruments is emerging structurally stronger and more scalable business for Cello, and we remain confident of achieving our target of revenue of INR500 crores plus in financial year 27.
But I think, yes, Q1 looks a little challenging. So we are trading very cautiously because we have been impacted.
